title: `restic check --read-data` does not list all broken packs

Output of `restic version`
--------------------------

Earlier (while the repository was damaged): `restic 0.9.6 compiled with go1.13.4 on linux/amd64`

When starting to investigate and repair damage: `restic 0.18.1 compiled with go1.25.1 on linux/amd64`

Repository format: 1

What backend/service did you use to store the repository?
---------------------------------------------------------

SFTP

Problem description / Steps to reproduce
----------------------------------------

1. Somehow break the repository, don't notice `check --read-data` errors for months.

2. The older Restic did not output the affected packs yet. So I manually ran a `sha256sum` one-liner on the `data` directory. It found following broken files:

restic repair snapshots --forget

9. Run another `sha256sum` command line. It finds following broken files in `data`:

```
./74/743112bb288ca8dfc7f9722b2c5c9b13d668e12236bd456e42dac86180f490f8
./80/80a464e5319c3492104c568b9287340d49cc50a00698c9fd37a54583bfb20f17

./d1/d181acb2904244c14331d336910ffd5e611dbb667dd0c983580724bfbe797147
```

Note that pack `ce8d0b612b5227055d7a4df97904c47f7dd42d42907e3c682ac62d5e0b474ad2` is missing in this list.

I can see that pack `ce8d0b612b5227055d7a4df97904c47f7dd42d42907e3c682ac62d5e0b474ad2` is already present in the backup before reproduction step 2.

   information to diagnose the problem!

 * The more time you spend describing an easy way to reproduce the behavior (if
   this is possible), the easier it is for the project developers to fix it!
-->

Expected behavior
-----------------

`restic check --read-data` should output all faulty packs. At least, when running commands suggested in its output and/or the troubleshooting guide, a subsequent `restic check --read-data` should succeed.

Actual behavior
---------------

`restic check --read-data` only outputs a subset of damaged pack files. The repair commands did not fully repair the repository.

Do you have any idea what may have caused this?
-----------------------------------------------

Why there were initially errors in the SFTP repository: Unreliable network connection. Backup target server restarts. I think the older Restic that created the backups did not yet support the atomic operation feature for SFTP, which could have prevented this.

During the checks and repair attempts, the network connection was stable though. So I think that there is some potential of improvement in the repair commands.

Did restic help you today? Did it make you happy in any way?
------------------------------------------------------------

I really appreciate the repair commands and the `--no-cache` option due to little disk space!

Even more I thank for the continuous maintenance of this tool!

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hi @reporter,

what happened between your first and your second post?

The message "no blobs found for pack 80a464e5319c3492104c568b9287340d49cc50a00698c9fd37a54583bfb20f17" clearly indicates that this packfile contained no valid blobs, according to the index. These packfiles might indeed have had a faulty ``sha256sum``, but ``restic repair`` removed them from the repository.

Your ``restic check`` runs for more than 13.5 hours, how large is your repository? I guess ~250GiB. Does it contain a lot of textual data? Then compression might help you to reduce the size of the repository. If however you have a lot of binary data like pdf, jpg, mov, mp4, ... compression will not be your best friend.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Thanks for your quick response! 

What would you like to do next? 

- Convert the repository into a version 2 repository (``restic migrate``)? Preferably with a larger standard pack size, something along the lines of the current default = 16 MiB. Your current effective pack size is about 1.7 MiB. By pruning with a larger packsize you would get < ~10k packfiles instead of your current ~75k. Before you commit yourself, always use ``prune --dry-run`` to see the effects. With an effective data rate of about ~2.5 MiB/s it will take a very long time for the ``restic  prune`` to run, but you can limit a run by using ``--max-repack-size``. Take into account that every blob has to be read and written back. If the upload- and download-performance differ, you might want to do a proper performance test.

- Alternatively you can stay with your version 1 repository and prune it at leisure to a higher packfile size.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Thanks for your reply. A few comments:
> The number of index files was also at a worrying 39k. 

You can always run ``restic repair index``to keep the number of index files under control. The size of the index files depends solely on the number of blobs (tree+data) in your repository. Use ~50 bytes per entry as a rough measure for size of an entry and you have the size of your index files. A fully populated index file is around 2 MiB in size.

> Still, I think the GitHub issue should remain open, because in the future it could save time for others if Restic would list the all the broken packs at the beginning.

I absolutely agree with you - ``restic check`` must list all broken packfiles.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
> You can always run `restic repair index`to keep the number of index files under control.

Please only use `restic prune` that will already automatically maintain the index. `restic repair index` should mostly be limited to damaged repositories.

The restic commands will be much faster if you omit the `--no-cache ` option.

> removing invalid index 4f327496d13fb8c5ccedddb701a2950244f677ba8b28f7a1ce9f5ad75d1c2cb6: LoadRaw(<ind
ex/4f327496d1>): invalid data returned

The sftp backend doesn't support fsync. The atomic rename feature is sufficient to handle cases where the client fails during the upload. But in case the server fails to actually write the data to disk, we might see the above error message.

> no blobs found for pack [...]

This simply means that the pack file are not contained in the repository index. Those files are only reported when passing `--verbose` to check. There is a `additional files were found in the repo` message, however, that is hidden when the repository is damaged otherwise. Additional files are automatically cleaned up by `prune`.

The only unexpected behavior is for `ce8d0b612b5227055d7a4df97904c47f7dd42d42907e3c682ac62d5e0b474ad2`. That looks like the index repair doesn't properly handle cases where the blobs of a pack file are spread over multiple indexes (yes that was unfortunately possible in restic 0.9.6 and a few later versions)

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
What has happened is the following: since restic 0.17.0, any operation that rewrites the index is no longer able to handle cases where the blobs of a pack file are split across multiple index files. Since then an index rewrite leads to a partial loss of one of those index entries.

`repair pack` unfortunately also didn't repair the index entry before extracting the pack file such that the data in the pack file is partially lost. https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21827 fixes that particular problem.

I'll also fix the index rewrite to prevent index data loss in this case.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21828 turns the original `pack ce8d0b612b5227055d7a4df97904c47f7dd42d42907e3c682ac62d5e0b474ad2 contained in several indexes: {0ff67749 b0a986a8}` warning into an error. The pack ID has to be passed to `repair packs` to fix the index.

Triggering the bug requires a very special constellation:
- restic < 0.10.0 in rare cases incorrectly splits the information about a pack file across multiple indexes . This implicitly means that only repositories using repository format version 1 can be affected.
- repository must accumulate actual pack file damage
- Neither `prune` or `repair index` are run using a restic version < 0.17.0
- Upgrade to restic >= 0.17.0
- Run `restic check`. Now due to the pack file damage you're prompted to run `repair packs` instead of `repair index`.
